blocks.text: Imagine working on a project with multiple team members, each making changes to the codebase simultaneously. How do you ensure everyone's changes are integrated smoothly without overwriting each other's work?

blocks.markdown: Version control systems (VCS) are essential tools in software engineering for managing changes to source code over time. They enable multiple developers to collaborate on a project by keeping track of every modification to the code in a special kind of database.

blocks.title: Version Control System
blocks.text: A version control system is a tool that helps manage changes to source code by recording modifications in a repository. It allows multiple developers to work on a project simultaneously without conflict.

blocks.markdown: One of the most powerful features of a VCS is branching. Branching allows developers to diverge from the main line of development and continue to work independently without affecting the main codebase until they are ready to merge their changes back.

blocks.title: Branching
blocks.text: Branching is the process of creating a separate line of development in a version control system, allowing developers to work on different features or fixes independently.

blocks.title: Creating and Using a Branch
blocks.prompt: Suppose you are working on a new feature for a project. How would you create and use a branch in Git?

steps.text: First, ensure you are on the main branch by executing the command:
Create a new branch for the feature:
Work on the feature and commit changes as needed.
Merge the feature branch back into the main branch once the feature is complete and tested.

blocks.answer: Creating and using a branch involves checking out the main branch, creating and switching to a new branch, working on the feature, and merging the branch back into the main branch.

blocks.markdown: While branching allows for parallel development, it can lead to merge conflicts when two branches modify the same part of the code. A merge conflict occurs when Git cannot automatically resolve differences between branches.

blocks.title: Merge Conflict
blocks.text: A merge conflict arises when changes from different branches cannot be automatically reconciled by the version control system. It requires manual intervention to resolve.

blocks.title: Resolving a Merge Conflict
blocks.prompt: You encounter a merge conflict while merging a feature branch into the main branch. How do you resolve it?

steps.text: Identify the files with conflicts using:
Open the conflicting files in a text editor and look for conflict markers (e.g., <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>).
Manually edit the files to resolve the conflicts, choosing which changes to keep.
After resolving conflicts, mark the files as resolved:
Complete the merge process by committing the resolved changes:

blocks.answer: Resolving a merge conflict involves identifying conflicting files, manually editing them to resolve conflicts, marking them as resolved, and committing the changes.

blocks.markdown: A well-maintained commit history is crucial for debugging and understanding the evolution of a project. Each commit should be a logical unit of work with a clear message describing the changes made.

blocks.title: Good Commit Message
blocks.text: A good commit message is concise yet descriptive. For example: 'Fix bug in user login validation logic.'

points: Version control systems manage changes to source code and support collaboration.
Branching allows parallel development but can lead to merge conflicts.
A clear commit history aids in debugging and understanding project changes.
